key_insight: A conditional diffusion model can synthesize realistic spatiotemporal turbulent flame evolution from experimental OH-PLIF and PIV data, including unseen flame transition events.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-driven surrogate for exploring flame dynamics in sparse experimental regimes, helping complement combustor testing and CFD studies.
method: x-prediction flow matching for conditional generation
Pixel-based spatiotemporal transformer to generate full space-time slabs
Transition synthesis via time-varying mixing of attached/detached denoising velocities
evidence_signal: The generated flames preserved key flame features and space-time statistics, especially at large scales, while transition synthesis produced coherent liftoff and reattachment trajectories not seen in training.
watch_item: Performance degrades at high temporal frequencies and small spatial scales, so output quality may depend strongly on the chosen slab duration and resolution.
paper_title: Generating synthetic evolution of turbulent flames with an experimental data-based spatiotemporal diffusion model
